level.title: Web Fundamentals
level.description: Learn how the internet and websites work in very simple and beginner-friendly language.

lessons.title: What Is The Internet?

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: The internet is a giant connection between millions of computers around the world that allows them to share information with each other.

theory.title: Understanding The Internet In Simple Words

sections.heading: Think About WhatsApp
sections.content: When you send a message on WhatsApp, your phone sends data through the internet to another person's phone. This is possible because both devices are connected to the internet.

sections.heading: Internet Is Like Roads
sections.content: Imagine roads connecting different cities. In the same way, the internet connects computers and devices together so they can communicate.

sections.heading: What Travels On The Internet?
sections.content: Messages, videos, photos, websites, games, and files all travel through the internet.

sections.heading: Devices Talk Using Rules
sections.content: Computers follow special communication rules called protocols so they can understand each other properly.

easyExample.title: Real Life Example
easyExample.content: When you open YouTube and watch a video, your phone requests the video from YouTube servers through the internet.

terms.meaning: Information like videos, text, or images

summary: Apps and websites use the internet

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: A website is a collection of pages stored on a computer called a server and opened through a browser.

sections.heading: What Happens When You Open Google?
sections.content: When you type google.com in your browser, your browser asks Google's server for the website files.

sections.heading: What Is A Browser?
sections.content: A browser is an app used to open websites. Chrome, Edge, Safari, and Firefox are browsers.

sections.heading: What Is A Server?
sections.content: A server is a powerful computer that stores website files and sends them to users when requested.

sections.heading: What Does The Browser Receive?
sections.content: The browser receives files like HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, and videos to display the website.

sections.heading: How Does The Website Appear?
sections.content: The browser reads the files and builds the website visually on your screen.

easyExample.title: Food Delivery Example
easyExample.content: Think of the browser as a customer and the server as a restaurant kitchen. The customer orders food, and the kitchen prepares and sends it back.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: DNS helps browsers find websites by converting website names into computer addresses called IP addresses.

sections.heading: Why DNS Is Needed
sections.content: Computers understand numbers better than names. But humans remember names more easily. DNS connects both together.

sections.heading: What Is A Domain Name?
sections.content: A domain name is the website name you type, like google.com or youtube.com.

sections.heading: What Is An IP Address?
sections.content: An IP address is the actual address of a server on the internet.

sections.heading: What Happens Internally?
sections.content: When you type a website name, DNS finds the correct IP address so the browser knows where to send the request.

easyExample.title: Phone Contact Example
easyExample.content: Your phone contacts save names like Mom or Friend, but internally they store phone numbers. DNS works the same way.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: The client asks for information and the server provides it.

sections.heading: What Is A Client?
sections.content: A client is usually your browser or mobile app that requests data.

sections.heading: What Is A Server?
sections.content: A server processes requests and sends back data like webpages, images, or videos.

sections.heading: Frontend And Backend
sections.content: Frontend is what users see on the screen. Backend handles logic, data, and server operations.

sections.heading: How They Work Together
sections.content: The client sends requests through the internet, and the server responds with the requested information.

easyExample.title: Restaurant Example
easyExample.content: You are the client ordering food, and the kitchen is the server preparing and sending your order.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: HTTP is the communication method used by browsers and servers to exchange information on the web.

sections.heading: What Does HTTP Do?
sections.content: HTTP allows browsers and servers to communicate with each other.

sections.heading: What Is A Request?
sections.content: A request is a message sent from the browser asking for something.

sections.heading: What Is A Response?
sections.content: A response is the data sent back from the server.

sections.heading: GET And POST
sections.content: GET is used to receive data. POST is used to send data.

sections.heading: Status Codes
sections.content: Servers send status codes to tell if the request worked successfully or failed.

easyExample.title: Ordering Food Example
easyExample.content: Your order to a restaurant is the request, and the food returned to you is the response.
